newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada consumer confidence dips in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Canada consumer confidence dips in third quarter.

text.p: Canada's consumer confidence dipped slightly in the third quarter as Canadians continued to fret about future job prospects, a private research organization said in a report issued on Tuesday.

The Conference Board of Canada's Autumn 1996 Index of Consumer Attitudes was down slightly from 101.4 in the second quarter to 100.8 in the third quarter, while the Index of Business Confidence dropped 0.8 index points to level off at 148.3.
Both surveys were conducted in September 1996.

"Canadians just don't see the job market improving, and they remain nervous about their own financial positions since few households have seen their income improve," said Paul Darby, director of the board's economic services group.
"Almost 27 percent of respondents felt their financial position had worsened over the last six months - which further emphasizes the financial security of Canadians," Darby said.
Regionally, only British Columbia and Ontario posted increases in consumer confidence. The index in B.C. rose 4.2 points to 102, while Ontario jumped 0.9 points to 105.
Respondents from both provinces felt it was a good time to make major purchases, according to the survey.
Quebec suffered the biggest decline - six points to 92.9 - but Atlantic Canada continues to carry the lowest index of consumer confidence, 84, amid fears of a worsening job market in the region.
Overall, however, fewer respondents expect financial hardship during the next six months. "Declining interest rates will help Canadians feel more in control of their finances," Darby said.
The Conference Board of Canada is an independent, non-profit research institution.
